questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Which list matches the differentiating features in arthritis at the chapter start?
opts: Articular/periarticular, inflammatory/non-inflammatory, axial/peripheral, acute/chronic, small/large joints, upper/lower/combined limbs, symmetry and number of joints
questions.exp: The approach lists articular versus periarticular, inflammatory versus non-inflammatory, axial versus peripheral, acute <6 weeks versus chronic >6 weeks, small versus large joints, upper/lower/combined involvement, symmetrical/asymmetrical involvement and number of joints. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
opts: Monoarthritis 1 joint, oligoarthritis 1–4 joints, polyarthritis ≥5 joints
Monoarthritis 2 joints, oligoarthritis 5–10 joints, polyarthritis >10 joints
Monoarthritis 0 joints, oligoarthritis exactly 5 joints, polyarthritis exactly 6 joints
All definitions require only axial joints
questions.exp: The number-of-joints branch defines monoarthritis as 1 joint, oligoarthritis 1–4 joints and polyarthritis ≥5 joints. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: A patient has localized point tenderness away from the capsule along the tendon line and pain mainly on active movement against gravity. Which category fits?
questions.exp: Periarticular disease has localized point tenderness, pain away from the joint capsule along tendon/bony prominences and painful active movement against gravity. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Deep diffuse pain near the joint with painful passive and active movements plus crepitation, locking, deformity, instability or swelling points to what?
questions.exp: Articular arthritis has deep diffuse pain, pain in the vicinity of the joint, both passive and active painful movements, and additional crepitation/locking/deformity/instability/swelling. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Which inflammatory arthritis feature and synovial-fluid threshold are printed?
opts: Morning stiffness <5 minutes worsened by activity and WBC <200 cells/µL
Pain only at night with no lab changes
Synovial urate crystals as the sole differentiator
Morning stiffness >45 minutes relieved by activity, worsened by rest, and synovial WBC >2000 cells/µL
questions.exp: Inflammatory arthritis has early morning stiffness >45 minutes, relieved with activity and worsened by rest; synovial fluid WBC >2000 cells/µL is best to differentiate inflammatory versus non-inflammatory. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Which structure note is printed for RA versus OA?
opts: RA involves synovium; OA involves articular cartilage and stiffness worsens with activity
RA involves cartilage only; OA involves synovium only
RA and OA both spare joints
questions.exp: The note states the structure involved in RA is synovium and in OA is articular cartilage, with joint stiffness worsening with activity. (Book p519)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Which predominant-joint pattern is printed for RA?
opts: Peripheral predominant RA with peripheral joints plus C-spine
Axial predominant RA involving spine plus shoulder and hip root joints
questions.exp: Types based on predominant joints list peripheral predominant RA as peripheral joints plus C-spine. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Inflammatory arthritis presents as monoarthritis. Which two diagnoses does the source flowchart first split to?
opts: Post-viral parvovirus B19 and undifferentiated arthritis
Septic arthritis and acute crystal arthropathy
questions.exp: The approach to inflammatory arthritis splits monoarthritis into septic arthritis and acute crystal arthropathy, which then branches to gout and pseudogout. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Which pair is printed as erosive arthritis in the table?
opts: Acute crystal arthropathies and Jaccoud arthropathy
questions.exp: The erosive arthritis column includes RA, psoriatic arthritis, chronic crystal arthropathy, CTDs including mixed CTDs and sarcoidosis, multicentric reticulohistiocytosis and Rhupus. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: Which pair is printed as non-erosive arthritis in the table?
opts: SLE/SLE-like arthritis and acute rheumatic fever Jaccoud arthropathy
questions.exp: The non-erosive column includes SLE/SLE-like arthritis, acute rheumatic fever Jaccoud arthropathy, relapsing polychondritis, Behcet disease and acute crystal arthropathies. (Book p520)

questions.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
questions.q: The MAGIC syndrome note in the arthritis approach means what?
opts: Behcet disease plus relapsing polychondritis with mouth and genital ulcers and inflamed cartilage
questions.exp: MAGIC syndrome is Behcet disease plus relapsing polychondritis, with mouth and genital ulcers and inflamed cartilage. (Book p520)

units.title: 1. Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
units.sec: Differentiating arthritis patterns and inflammatory arthritis
units.guide:
The arthritis approach starts with differentiating axes: articular/periarticular, inflammatory/non-inflammatory, axial/peripheral and joint count.
Articular versus periarticular pain, inflammatory arthritis lab/synovial findings and RA/OA structures are kept together.
Predominant-joint, inflammatory-arthritis flowchart, erosion table and MAGIC note complete the brief chapter.
